conviction_note: Findings sum to +5.1, but two haircuts get applied on top and the note states them: (a) the date is NOT company-confirmed and TRT has never pre-announced one in its entire filing history — WallStreetZen carries 2026-09-18 while Investing.com/other aggregators point at 2026-09-21, and 09-18 would be the EARLIEST fiscal-year print in nine years of record (2025-09-19 is the earliest ever; median is 09-24) — so I put P(print lands in the 09-18 window) at roughly 0.45; (b) the stock is already +12.46% over 5 days on the 09-17 automotive-contract release and the Nasdaq debut, which is sell-the-news risk worth about 15% of the thesis. +5.1 x 0.85 x 0.45 = +1.9, rounded to +2.0. Conditional on the print actually landing on 09-18 I would be at roughly +4.3. The fundamental read (+7% vs a naive bar) is much larger than the reaction number, and the gap is entirely event-date probability plus this name's demonstrated habit of paying almost nothing for the FY print specifically (+0.55% on 2025-09-19) even though it paid +30.54% for the FQ3 print.
bar: UNSOURCED — there is no analyst estimate for TRT at all (stockanalysis.com shows analyst coverage and price target as 'n/a': https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/trt/), no company guidance of any kind, and no options market. Per my own rule every size on this name is therefore capped small. The bar I am sizing against is the naive one a reader would build off the last print: FQ3 revenue of $16.5m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774926016916/ex_963089.htm) extrapolated flat-to-modestly-up into FQ4, call it ~$18m. I estimate FQ4 at ~$19.5m, hence +7%.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 850,341 shares at the 2026-08-31 settlement date, DOWN 60,632 from the prior period; 8.4% of float; days to cover 4.88 on FINRA's average daily volume (https://equibles.com/stocks/trt/short-interest, and https://fintel.io/ss/us/trt for the same FINRA series). Against 10,112,599 shares outstanding (10-Q cover page, 2026-05-01: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774926016914/trt20260331_10q.htm) and a float reduced by insider blocks — Richard M. Horowitz alone still held 664,784 shares after selling 67,500 at $18.10 on 2026-05-18 — 850k short is a genuinely crowded position in a name that turns over only ~$1.63m/day. There is NO OPTIONS MARKET (baseline status no_options_market), so there is no skew, no implied move, and critically no way for a short to hedge: covering means buying stock in a thin tape. That is a squeeze mechanism in its own right and it is the main reason I have shrunk both of my negative findings and kept the net sign positive. The baseline gives me no directional statement from the option market at all, so I am working without the anchor the stage normally leans on, and I say so.

findings.finding: FQ4 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026) should print a record ~$19-20m of revenue, taking FY2026 to roughly $67m against FY2025's $36.5m (+~83%) and flipping the full year from a $(0.01) diluted loss to a profit — the June quarter is structurally TRT's largest, the $5.3m (March) and $2.5m (by mid-May) AI-GPU burn-in-board orders ship into it, and the 104,000 sq ft Perai/Penang facility commenced 2026-06-01.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is precisely the line TRT pays for. On 2026-05-14 the FQ3 release led with '124% Q3 Revenue Growth' and the stock rose +30.54% despite an $81k OPERATING LOSS and a net loss to common — the baseline's largest move by an order of magnitude. The other five reactions in the baseline are +2.12, +3.37, +0.55, -6.23, -1.13, i.e. revenue-growth shocks get paid and nothing else does. The counterweight, which I have applied rather than merely noted: the single FY print in the baseline (2025-09-19) moved only +0.55%, so the annual release is historically this name's quietest, and that is why this sits at +4.0 and not at the +30 the name has shown it can do.
findings.why_not_priced: Zero analysts cover TRT, so no one has published a FQ4 or FY2026 number anywhere — there is literally no estimate for the market to hold. If this arithmetic were in the price, the 20-day run-up would not be -0.35% (flat) and the stock would not be sitting 43.7% below its 52-week high; a market that had assembled '$67m revenue, +83%, return to profit' would not leave a $114m market cap at ~1.7x that revenue with 8.4% of the float short. The inputs are public (a May press release and four order releases), but nobody has done the join, which on a zero-coverage name is exactly the condition under which a pre-determined number still moves the stock.
findings.independence: Four separate primary documents point the same way and are NOT the same document as the source above: the FY2025 release giving the FQ4 comp of $10.7m and full-year $36.5m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774925029456/ex_862911.htm, 2025-09-19); the 8-K disclosing the Skygate Technology (M) Sdn Bhd lease of ~104,000 sq ft at Perai, Penang, term commencing 2026-06-01 at ~$115k/month (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774926014620/trt20260504_8k.htm, 2026-05-04); and the order releases of 2026-06-04 ($2.6m, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260604342334/en/Trio-Tech-International-Receives-Additional-$2.6-Million-in-Orders-for-Burn-In-Boards-Supporting-Next-Generation-AI-GPU-Platform) and 2026-07-28 ($3.8m, cumulative $14.2m since March). Note per lesson 4: the April $10m registered direct at $9.50 is the financing leg of this same ramp — the money bought the Penang capacity and working capital against $14.2m of announced orders, so it is corroborated demand rather than distress, and I have folded it into THIS finding rather than filing it separately, because it is one fact.
findings.net_of_rest_of_company: This rests on the Semiconductor Back-End Solutions segment (78% of FQ3 revenue, $13.1m of $16.5m). The other 22% — Industrial Electronics — grew +76% YoY in FQ3 and +40% for the nine months, and was the segment that carried FQ4 FY2025 (+70% YoY). So the rest of the company is growing too and there is no offsetting drag to net against; if anything IE adds to the FQ4 comp rather than subtracting.

findings.finding: FY2026 gross margin will print at roughly 16-17% against 25% in FY2025, and full-year operating income will land near FY2025's $254k despite revenue nearly doubling — the 10-K makes it visible for the first time that ~$30m of incremental revenue produced approximately zero incremental operating profit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has explicitly refused to pay attention to this line once already, at the same magnitude: the 2026-05-14 release disclosed 15.5% gross margin against 26.8% a year earlier and an operating loss, and the stock rose +30.54%. Nine-month operating income of $62k against FY2025's full-year $254k was in the same document. The shareholder base has been shown this exact number and bought it.
findings.why_not_priced: Resolved rather than sized as written (lesson 3): the honest reading is that this is ~90% dead as a negative, because the market saw it in May and paid +30%. What survives is only the difference in frame — a 10-K presents the full-year mix shift and the flat operating income as an annual fact rather than one quarter's noise, and the FY release is the one print of the year that arrives with risk factors attached. That residual is worth a few tenths, not a point, and I have sized it that way rather than writing a -1.0 and then rebutting it in the next sentence. If it were fully priced there would be a published margin discussion somewhere; there is none, which is the only reason it is not zero.
findings.independence: Shares its underlying document set with finding 1 (the same FQ3 release and 10-Q), so it is a second reading of one filing and must not be counted as independent corroboration. The one genuinely separate input is the FY2025 release showing the 25% full-year gross margin and $254k operating income it is being measured against (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774925029456/ex_862911.htm). Sized down further per lesson 7 because 8.4% of the float is short.

findings.finding: TRT disclosed a two-stage ransomware plus data-exfiltration incident at a Singapore subsidiary under Item 1.05 on 2026-03-20 (encryption 2026-03-11, unauthorised disclosure of Company data 2026-03-18), said only that it was not material to the quarter ended 2026-03-31, and has filed NO 8-K/A since — so the FY2026 10-K is the first full accounting of remediation cost, insurance recovery and Singapore PDPA exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name — TRT has never disclosed a cyber incident before, so there is no reaction history for this line. Sized as a one-off with no path to a guide accordingly (lesson 2), at a small fraction of what the same dollars would be worth as operating profit. For scale, the nearest analogue in the baseline is the 2025-05-13 print at -6.23%, which was a revenue-decline reaction, not a one-off.
findings.why_not_priced: I could not find a single news story, aggregator entry or analyst note referencing this Item 1.05 anywhere — the wire picked up every one of TRT's order announcements and the Nasdaq transfer, and skipped this entirely. If it were priced there would be a story, a risk-factor discussion, or at minimum a StockTitan headline, and there is none. The 8-K's own language left the door open ('could result in a future determination that the incident may be material') and the company has neither closed it with an amendment nor quantified it in six months.
findings.independence: none — this rests on one document and nothing else in the public record corroborates or contradicts it, which is itself the point. Kept deliberately small for that reason, and shrunk further because 8.4% of float short makes any negative on this name expensive to hold (lesson 7).

findings.finding: 850,341 shares short at the 2026-08-31 FINRA settlement — 8.4% of float, 4.88 days to cover — in a name with no options market to hedge in and only ~$1.63m/day of turnover, three days after it moved to the Nasdaq Global Market and into a release whose likely headline is 'revenue up ~80%, return to full-year profitability'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-14 +30.54% is the direct precedent for what a squeeze looks like in this name: a revenue headline into a thin tape with no options to hedge, producing a move eleven times the median reaction of 2.75%. The baseline's own max_abs_move_pct of 30.54 against a median of 2.75 is the signature of a positioning-driven tape rather than a fundamentals-driven one.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest publishes twice a month with a nine-day lag and carries no options surface to read it off, so on a zero-coverage $114m name there is no mechanism by which this is in the price — no put skew to reflect it, no analyst note to flag it, no borrow-rate headline. If the market had priced a squeeze the 20-day run-up would not be -0.35% and the stock would not be 43.7% below its 52-week high. The short position is also already declining (-60,632 in the period), which is covering under way rather than conviction being added.
findings.independence: Corroborated by a separate FINRA-derived source (https://fintel.io/ss/us/trt) carrying the same 850,341 figure and the 4.88 days-to-cover. Independent of findings 1-3 in mechanism: those are about what the number will be, this is about who has to buy if it is good. It is an amplifier of finding 1 rather than an addition to it, which is why it is sized at less than half of it rather than summed at face value.

outside_window.finding: The three-year automotive burn-in contract announced 2026-09-17 with a $4.7m minimum commitment (scalable to ~$6m) and the $3.8m of AI-GPU board orders announced 2026-07-28 are FY2027 revenue almost in their entirety — they cannot appear in a fiscal year that ended 2026-06-30, and the company gives no guidance, so nothing about them resolves on 09-18 beyond a sentence of commentary.

TRT adopted Third Amended and Restated Bylaws effective 2026-07-07 adding advance-notice nomination procedures, Rule 14a-19 universal-proxy mechanics and exclusive-forum provisions — a defensive package adopted mid-year rather than at an annual meeting, while a 13D holder (Richard M. Horowitz) has been selling down. Any consequence runs to the December 2026 annual meeting and the nomination window, not to this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: A company source confirming ANY earnings date. TRT has never pre-announced one in its entire EDGAR history — no 8-K, no press release, ever. The IR page (https://www.triotech.com/investor-relations/) shows nothing past May 2026 and does not even carry the August/September press releases, so it cannot be used to rule anything in or out. WallStreetZen says 2026-09-18; Investing.com-sourced results point at 2026-09-21. This is the single largest uncertainty on the name and it is unresolvable from public sources.

The Form 25 / 8-A12B / CERT trio of 2026-09-15 — chased and RESOLVED, and it is not what the form names suggest. It is a voluntary UPGRADE, not a delisting: the 8-K of 2026-08-19 (items 3.01/8.01) and its exhibit 99.1 disclose a transfer from NYSE American to the Nasdaq Global Market, last day on NYSE MKT 2026-09-15, first day on Nasdaq 2026-09-16, ticker unchanged. It was announced a month ago on the wire and is fully priced; it produces no finding. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/732026/000143774926028480/ex_1006326.htm

Any unannounced negative in the order book — every order release (2026-03, 2026-05, 2026-06-04 $2.6m, 2026-07-28 $3.8m, 2026-09-17 $4.7m) went out on BusinessWire and was picked up by Investing.com, Nasdaq, Yahoo and MarketScreener. All priced.

A shelf or ATM that could dilute into the print — the only S-3 is from 2025-11-03 (amended 2025-12-12); the April 2026 $10m registered direct was drawn off it and no new registration statement has been filed since. No 8-K/A, no NT 10-K, no going-concern language found.

Insider activity in the exit window — the last Form 4 is 2026-07-29 and nothing has been filed in August or September 2026. Horowitz's selling (67,500 shares at $18.10 on 2026-05-18, leaving 664,784) is four months stale and already inside the drawdown from $21.38.

Job postings, app-store data and customer-forum chatter — TRT is a B2B contract test-services house in Singapore/Malaysia/Thailand with no consumer surface and no scrapeable hiring page that resolves before the print.
Any evidence the December 2025 2-for-1 forward split or the January 2026 charter amendment has an unresolved consequence — both are complete and reflected in the 10,112,599 share count.
baseline_tension: Nothing in the baseline argues against me and nothing in it supports me either — there is no options market, therefore no skew and no priced_lean, so the market makes no directional statement on this name at all, and the -0.35% 20-day run-up says the price is where it was a month ago despite an 80%-revenue-growth year having finished; my findings cut WITH that emptiness rather than against a stated market view, and the only baseline fact that genuinely pushes back is that the one FY print in the six-event history moved +0.55%, which is why +5.1 of findings becomes +2.0 of expected move.
lessons_applied: Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves MORE, and understatement is the systematic error): raised finding 1 from +3.0 to +4.0 and widened its high to +12.0. I had sized a zero-analyst, zero-options, 66%-realised-vol name whose own history contains a +30.54% below its median reaction, which is exactly the error the rule names.

Lesson 6 (unsourced bar caps every size) held finding 1 back from going further than +4.0 — I genuinely cannot source a consensus because none exists, so the cap binds and I have said so in `bar`. These two rules pulled in opposite directions and +4.0 is where they meet.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): finding 2 as drafted was self-rebutting — I wrote -1.0 for the gross-margin collapse and then noted the market had seen the same 15.5% margin in May and bought it +30%. Resolved rather than sized: cut to -0.4 and the text now carries the resolution instead of the rebuttal.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative): 8.4% of float and 4.88 days to cover with no options to hedge in cut finding 3 from -0.5 to -0.3 as well.
Lesson 2 (size one-offs as one-offs): re-filed the cybersecurity incident from a vague negative to `lands_on: one_off` with no path to a guide, which is the reason it sits at a few tenths.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): I had left the April $10m registered direct out entirely. Asked what the money buys — a 104,000 sq ft Penang facility commencing 2026-06-01 against $14.2m of announced AI-GPU orders — got the 'funds visible demand' answer, and folded it into finding 1's independence rather than filing it as a fifth finding, because per the 'two readings of one document' rule it is the same fact.

Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): added an explicit net-of-the-rest line to finding 1 — SBS is 78% of revenue and Industrial Electronics, the other 22%, grew +76% YoY, so there is nothing to net against.

Net effect: impact sum +3.0 -> +5.1, expected move +1.6 -> +2.0. The expected move moved far less than the sum because the event-date probability and the sell-the-news haircut are both unchanged by the file — they were in the draft and survived it.
